generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, creativity is a working graduate attribute, not an ornament. The problems the discipline cares about, designing an intervention that people will actually use, measuring something that resists direct observation, making sense of a messy dataset, rarely come with a settled method. Innovation is what moves them forward, adaptability is what keeps the response fit as constraints emerge, and employers of psychology graduates name exactly these capabilities.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two final-year psychology students are asked, in a careers task, to describe how creativity features in applied psychology.

Tom writes that psychologists need to be creative thinkers and that creativity is valued in any profession. The claim is true but generic. It names creativity as a good thing without saying what problem it solves or how it would show up in practice, so it would read the same on an application in any field.

Amara identifies a recurring problem with no routine solution, that is, engaging reluctant clients in a therapeutic programme, and argues that this is where creativity earns its place: designing an unfamiliar approach, then adapting it as the client responds. Creativity is tied to a concrete problem, linked to adaptability, and expressed as enterprise rather than as a personality trait.

Both value creativity. Only Amara appraises it as an attribute: named, located in a real psychological problem, and argued for in the terms the profession would recognise.
generatedProse.summary: Creativity earns its place among the graduate attributes psychology prizes because it generates workable options for problems that have no settled method, from intervention design to making sense of difficult data, and because that habit transfers into professional practice. You can now appraise creativity as an attribute, relate it to adaptability and flexibility, and articulate how it shows up in psychology. The next lesson turns creativity onto how you regulate your own learning.

check.body: You are arguing that creativity matters in psychology. Which move best shows creativity as a graduate attribute?

items.text: Naming a real problem in psychology that has no routine solution and showing how a new option would address it.
Stating that psychologists should be more creative.
Listing creativity among your strengths without an example.
Avoiding any psychological problem that looks too difficult.

feedback.correct: That's right. In psychology, naming a problem with no routine solution and showing a new option argues creativity as an attribute.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for the option that ties creativity to a concrete problem in psychology.
feedback.incorrectFinal: The attribute is argued by locating it in a real psychological problem and a new option for it. Exhortation, bare lists and avoidance do not.
